::: {.key-question}
What external factors influence health and wellbeing for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people and families in the NEPHU catchment, including in supporting children and strong families?
:::

## All Admissions

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hospitalisations - total admissions
# Data from PHIDU Social Health Atlas
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in PHIDU data
hospital_total <- f_read_phidu_iare_hospital(data_sheet    = "Admissions_sex",
                                             column_select = "total_admissions_excluding_same_day_admissions_for_renal_dialysis_aboriginal_persons")

# Data wrangling
hospital_total <- hospital_total %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(iare_name = factor(iare_name, levels = iare_inc_vic_lvl)) %>%
  #
  dplyr::arrange(iare_name)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [PHIDU Social Health Atlas](https://phidu.torrens.edu.au/social-health-atlases), compiled from the [Victorian Admitted Episodes Dataset (VAED)](https://www.health.vic.gov.au/data-reporting/victorian-admitted-episodes-dataset).

- During the four-year period 01 July 2017 to 30 June 2021 there were 44,104 hospital admissions for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne.

- The number of admissions for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 5,874 (Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea IARE) to 733 (Whitehorse IARE).

- The age-standardised rate of admissions for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 34,280 per 100,000 population (Melbourne/Port Phillip IARE) to 21,370 per 100,000 population (Knox IARE).

- 5 of the 10 IAREs in the NEPHU catchment area had an age-standardised admission rate above the average rate for all Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne (Melbourne/Port Phillip, Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea, Moreland/Broadmeadows, Craigieburn/Sunbury, and Whitehorse IAREs).

::: {.callout-tip title="Definitions and notes about this topic" icon=false collapse=false}

## Acute Potentially Preventable Conditions

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hospitalisations - acute preventable admissions
# Data from PHIDU Social Health Atlas
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in PHIDU data
hospital_acute <- f_read_phidu_iare_hospital(data_sheet    = "Admissions_acute_prev",
                                             column_select = "admissions_for_total_acute_conditions_aboriginal_people")

# Data wrangling
hospital_acute <- hospital_acute %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(iare_name = factor(iare_name, levels = iare_inc_vic_lvl)) %>%
  #
  dplyr::arrange(iare_name)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [PHIDU Social Health Atlas](https://phidu.torrens.edu.au/social-health-atlases), compiled from the [Victorian Admitted Episodes Dataset (VAED)](https://www.health.vic.gov.au/data-reporting/victorian-admitted-episodes-dataset).

- During the four-year period 01 July 2017 to 30 June 2021 there were 2,247 hospital admissions for acute potentially preventable conditions for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne. Acute potentially preventable conditions includes conditions such as cellulitis, acute convulsions and epilepsy, dental conditions, ear nose and throat infections, eclampsia, gangrene, pelvic inflammatory disease, perforated/bleeding ulcers, pneumonia, and urinary tract infections.

- The number of admissions for acute potentially preventable conditions for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 340 (Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea IARE) to 34 (Maroondah IARE).

- The age-standardised rate of admissions for acute potentially preventable conditions for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 1,914 per 100,000 population (Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea IARE) to 1,015 per 100,000 population (Maroondah IARE).

- 3 of the 10 IAREs in the NEPHU catchment area had an age-standardised admission rate for acute potentially preventable conditions above the average rate for all Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne (Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea, Moreland/Broadmeadows, and Whitehorse IAREs).

::: {.callout-tip title="Definitions and notes about this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
- `r note_aboriginality_vaed`

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

`r note_caveat_admissions`

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

`r note_caveat_iare_ratio`
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="ICD-10-AM codes for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
Admissions for acute preventable conditions were defined as those with a principal diagnosis code in the following list, coded using the [International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems 10th Revision Australian Modification (ICD-10-AM)](https://www.ihacpa.gov.au/health-care/classification/icd-10-amachiacs):

  - Cellulitis: L02, L03, L04, L08, L88, L98.0, L98.3
  - Convulsions and epilepsy: G40, G41, R56
  - Dental conditions: K02, K03, K04, K05, K06, K08, K09.8, K09.9, K12, K13, K14.0
  - Ear, nose, and throat infections: H66, J02, J03, J06, J31.2
  - Eclampsia: O15
  - Gangrene: I70.2, R02
  - Pelvic inflammatory disease: N70, N73, N74
  - Perforated or bleeding ulcers: K25.0, K25.1, K25.2, K25.4, K25.5, K25.6, K26.0, K26.1, K26.2, K26.4, K26.5, K26.6, K27.0, K27.1, K27.2, K27.4, K27.5, K27.6, K28.0, K28.1, K28.2, K28.4, K28.5, K28.6
  - Pneumonia (not vaccine-preventable): J15.3, J15.4, J15.7, J16.0
  - Urinary tract infections (including pyelonephritis): N10, N11, N12, N13.6, N15.1, N15.9, N28.9, N39.0, N39.9

:::

## Chronic Potentially Preventable Conditions

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hospitalisations - chronic preventable admissions
# Data from PHIDU Social Health Atlas
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in PHIDU data
hospital_chronic <- f_read_phidu_iare_hospital(data_sheet    = "Admissions_chronic_prev",
                                               column_select = "admissions_for_total_chronic_conditions_aboriginal_people")

# Data wrangling
hospital_chronic <- hospital_chronic %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(iare_name = factor(iare_name, levels = iare_inc_vic_lvl)) %>%
  #
  dplyr::arrange(iare_name)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [PHIDU Social Health Atlas](https://phidu.torrens.edu.au/social-health-atlases), compiled from the [Victorian Admitted Episodes Dataset (VAED)](https://www.health.vic.gov.au/data-reporting/victorian-admitted-episodes-dataset).

- During the four-year period 01 July 2017 to 30 June 2021 there were 2,096 hospital admissions for chronic potentially preventable conditions for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne. Chronic potentially preventable conditions include chronic heart conditions, chronic lung conditions, diabetes, nutritional deficiencies, and hypertension.

- The number of admissions for chronic potentially preventable conditions for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 403 (Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea IARE) to 24 (Whitehorse IARE).

- The age-standardised rate of admissions for chronic potentially preventable conditions for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 2,682 per 100,000 population (Maroondah IARE) to 534 per 100,000 population (Melbourne East IARE).

- 4 of the 10 IAREs in the NEPHU catchment area had an age-standardised admission rate above the average rate for all Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne (Maroondah, Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea, Craigieburn/Sunbury, and Moreland/Broadmeadows IAREs).

::: {.callout-tip title="Definitions and notes about this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
- `r note_aboriginality_vaed`

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

`r note_caveat_admissions`

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

`r note_caveat_iare_ratio`
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="ICD-10-AM codes for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
Admissions for chronic preventable conditions were defined as those with a principal diagnosis code in the following list, coded using the [International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems 10th Revision Australian Modification (ICD-10-AM)](https://www.ihacpa.gov.au/health-care/classification/icd-10-amachiacs):

  - Angina: I20, I24.0, I24.8, I24.9
  - Asthma: J45, J46
  - Bronchiectasis: J20, J47
  - Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD): J41, J42, J43, J44
  - Congestive heart failure: I11.0, I50, J81
  - Diabetes complications: E10, E11, E13, E14
  - Hypertension: I10, I11.9
  - Iron deficiency anaemia: D50.1, D50.8, D50.9
  - Nutritional deficiencies: E40, E41, E42, E43, E55.0, E64.3
  - Rheumatic heart disease: I00, I01, I02, I05, I06, I07, I08, I09

:::
